Class SpringMappings

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.DefaultMappings
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringMappings
All Implemented Interfaces:
Mappings, MappingResourceTarget, Aware, BeanFactoryAware, SmartInitializingSingleton
public class SpringMappings extends DefaultMappings implements MappingResourceTarget, BeanFactoryAware, SmartInitializingSingleton
Mappings configured with Spring resources, and the bean to wire into a Spring application. 
<bean id="mappings" class="org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringMappings">
    <property name="mappingResources">
        <list>
            <value>classpath:gender.mapping.xml</value>
            <value>classpath:encounter.mapping.yaml</value>
        </list>
    </property>
</bean>
A resource is dispatched to a loader by its file extension, so the formats may be mixed freely - whichever modules are on the classpath decide which ones can be read. Where a name does not identify a format - a location without a file extension, a file called gender.xml - set mappingFormat to name one for this bean's resources, or pass it per resource to setMappingResource(Resource, String). Applications add further mappings on top with CustomMappings: this bean collects the MappingResourceHolder beans of the application context itself, so no configurer and no post processor is needed.

Collecting happens in afterSingletonsInstantiated(), i.e. once all singletons have been instantiated and before the ContextRefreshedEvent that starts e.g. the Camel context, so the mappings are complete when routes are built. They are not complete yet while singletons are being initialized: a @PostConstruct method sees only the resources set on this bean directly. Contributions can be ordered relative to each other with Spring's @Order / Ordered on the MappingResourceHolder bean.

Functions that a computed fallback names are a property of this bean, so they are registered while it is created - before any configurer adds a resource that refers to one. A module that ships both a mapping file and the functions it names should contribute a MappingFunctionProvider service instead, and needs no configuration at all.

This holds the model's constraints - and so does SpringBidiMappingService, which reads into one: a duplicate mapping name is an error unless the later declaration says override, and a value with two inverses is an error rather than a reverse lookup that silently answers whichever key was written last. Both can be relaxed with DefaultMappings.setAllowOverride(boolean) and DefaultMappings.setAllowReverseCollisions(boolean) for a source that cannot express the intent.

Since:
6.0

    • setMappingResource

      public void setMappingResource(Resource resource, String format)
      Reads one resource in a format named explicitly rather than left to its file extension.

      A resource that has been read before is skipped, which keeps this bean idempotent so that a contribution reaching it both directly and through a deprecated CustomMappingsConfigurer is only evaluated once.

      Parameters:
      resource - a mapping resource
      format - a format id such as xml or conceptmap-r4-json, or null to fall back to setMappingFormat(String) and then to the file extension
      See Also:
      • setMappingResource(Resource)

    • setMappingFunctions

      public void setMappingFunctions(Map<String, Function<String,String>> functions)
      Registers the functions that a mapping's computed fallback refers to by name, i.e. what <unmatched mode="function" ref="..."/> resolves against. A function receives the key that had no entry and returns the value for it, so a mapping can derive its answer from its input rather than list it.

      A mapping source naming a function that is not registered is rejected as it is read, so register them first. As a property of this bean that happens before any configurer adds a mapping resource - but a resource set on this bean itself is read as soon as it is set, so in a bean definition declare this property before mappingResources.

      Parameters:
      functions - functions by name, replacing any registered under the same name before
